Send one command to the experiment server and print the result.

Usage:
  python3 query.py describe                 list the rule dimensions and the input encoding (free)
  python3 query.py describe <task>          the task's response to every input, as one string (free)
  python3 query.py compare <task> <task>    fraction of inputs with the same response (free)
  python3 query.py budget                   remaining budget (free)
  python3 query.py train <task> [<task>...] train the learner on these tasks (cost 1 per task)
  python3 query.py test <task>              examples to criterion for this task, one noisy sample (cost 1)
  python3 query.py submit '<verdict JSON>'  submit your final verdict (free; ends the session)
Tasks are named like L1-S2-M3.

content.text:
I submitted **part-based** with 0.8 confidence. The answer came from a train-and-test transfer experiment run through `query.py`, which used 23 of the 60 paid queries. I didn't read the server's code.

Tasks that share parts also tend to give similar responses, so either learner type could explain transfer between them. To separate the two, I used the free `compare` command to choose training tasks:

| Target | What I trained on | Response overlap with target | Examples needed before → after (mean) |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1-S2-M3 | Tasks that together cover all 3 of its parts (L1-S1-M1, L2-S2-M2, L4-S4-M3) | Low (0, 0.06, 0.375) | ~50 → ~14 |
| L3-S3-M4 (control) | Tasks sharing no parts with it (L4-S2-M2, L4-S4-M2, L4-S1-M2) | Higher (0.56 each) | 42 → ~37 |

A holistic learner should benefit most from the high-overlap tasks. Instead the big gain came from shared parts, which is what a part-based learner predicts.

Limits on the result:
- **Noisy tests:** repeat tests on the same task after training ranged from 1 to 39 examples, so I averaged 6–7 samples per target.
- **Thin control baseline:** I have only one pre-training sample for the control target. If the true value was nearer 50, the control would show some transfer without shared parts.
- **No replication:** I only ran one part-sharing target. The other one I looked at, L2-S4-M1, also had high response overlap with the trained tasks, so it couldn't separate the two explanations.
